# Independent audit: all-menu exposed-target obstruction and selective simplex-facet payment

I read both
\`candidate 6df920a6fc1694e9\`
and
\`candidate 05d41ace8d693538\`.
Both pass in their stated scope. The counterexample is above OC and the selective facet theorem pays it; neither is a complete OC result.

## 1. The actual all-menu example

The finite base set, canonical fiber compatibility, within-fiber covariance, and smoothing error bounds check. The source-core bound follows from the three ordinary centroid directions and is sufficient for exact active-cap attainment and the full-normal moment uniqueness argument.

For a direction normalized to maximum vertex value two, the other values are \(-1\pm s\). Its one-vertex centroid cap area is \(18/(9-s^2)\). At \(|s|=1/4\) this is \(2+2/143\); the two-vertex case has area at least \(9/4\). The displacement error \(12\delta\) and \(13\delta<2/143\) therefore confine EVERY active continuous direction to the stated three cones.

The endpoint estimates are uniform across those cones. For the B/C cones, zero base tilt misses both endpoints, so active minimality forces zero endpoint capture for every actual active tilt. For the A cone, at least one endpoint is completely captured for every tilt, and finite saturation attains exactly its mass \(v\). Thus the endpoint coareas vanish for every active cap.

The three elementary separating vectors show that every balanced menu uses all three cones. Consequently no menu can have a common interior point on either exposed endpoint fiber. The exact response coefficient
\[
k_u=9(2-u\cdot y+h\Gamma(u)/2)/(9-s^2)
\]
has the stated normalization: \(S_{\rm normalized}u_{\rm normalized}=k_uu\). The interval \(1.9<k_u<2.1\) and the vertex dot products give total cone weight at most \(105/257<4/9\), hence also bound every response atom.

For quantile weights, converting from \(\Gamma\)-normalized normals to the displayed representatives first gives B/C weight at least \(8/13\). Converting back costs at most \(\sqrt{49/48}\), proving the explicit positive saturation-deficit bound. This is consistent with the simplex-base rank note because here the middle fiber STRICTLY contains the endpoint Minkowski average.

The full own-cone isolation obstruction is on positive-length shared normal patches, so it is not an artifact of isolated boundary points.

## 2. The selective simplex identity

For the vertex-i cap of a simplex, centroid of its section equal to \(y\) forces edge intercepts \(d y_j\), \(j\ne i\). Its cap fraction is \(q_i=d^d\prod_j y_j/y_i\). At this section-centroid configuration, the derivative with respect to the source agrees with the fixed-normal cap derivative: the first normal derivative vanishes. Thus the gradient calculation used for the actual response balance is legitimate.

If \(T_0=\sum_i\theta_iq_i\), balance on the barycentric-sum-one tangent space gives \(\theta_iq_i=T_0(1-dy_i)\). The positive circuit gives \(r_i=1-dy_i>0\), and normalizing yields the exact weights \(\theta_i=(r_i/q_i)/B\).

On facet \(F_i\), cap j has area fraction \(q_j/(d y_i)\) for \(j\ne i\), while cap i has zero area. Summing gives the identical facet average \(1/B\), independent of i. The algebraic inequality \(1/B\geq\Gamma_d\) is precisely the earlier archived inequality; its pairwise-averaging proof applies to this positive simplex of r values. For d=1 the quotient is identically one half.

The claim uses the ENTIRE constant-weight facet. It would not justify restriction to an arbitrary free patch.

## 3. Exact anchored-triangle payment and positive-width passage

The cap-area equality gives \(12t^2-4t+\alpha=0\), hence the root near one third is
\(t=(1+\sqrt{1-3\alpha})/6\). The response weights and the uniform free-facet fraction give
\[
4t^2/(6t-1)=4/9+4(3t-1)^2/[9(6t-1)]>4/9.
\]
The field \(\chi(n)[c-x_1]_+\) is globally finite, nonnegative and convex in the full point for each fixed normal. It equals a positive constant on the entire middle facet \(x_1=-1\) and vanishes on all other measured normal bundles, including the endpoint facets with \(x_1=c\).

The compact directional cones and the actual own-strip centroid identities identify every zero-width subsequential cap limit. Their response measures and facet capture consequently converge to the same value. The strict margin persists for sufficiently small h at fixed sigma. Its size is order sigma to the fourth power; no larger quantitative width window is silently inferred.

No correction is required.
